newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS - SLIPS ON OVERNIGHT CRUDE LOSS.
newsitem.headline: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS - SLIPS ON OVERNIGHT CRUDE LOSS.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps lost ground at midday on Thursday on overnight crude losses but with the market rebounding off its early morning lows as bargain hunters emerged, traders said.
"The market came off because of the overnight crude loss but the loss is not that big because we are approaching winter," a trader said.
Asian demand fo heating oil -- fuel oil, gas oil and kerosene -- reaches its peak in the winter season.
August gas oil was last quoted at $23.10/$23.25 per barrel, down from Wednesday's $23.35/$23.45. September was quoted at $23.60/$23.75, also down from Wednesday's $23.90/$24.00, brokers said.
September traded to a low of $23.50 in the morning before edging up to trade at $23.55 and was last quoted above this level, they said.
The August/September time spread was last quoted at minus 45 cents to minus 60 cents compared to Wednesday's trade of minus 60 cents, brokers said.
They said the narrowing of the contango was due to the current prompt physical support which is holding up August swap levels.
In the physical market on Wednesday, a 240,000-barrel cargo traded at $23.08 per barrel free-on-board Singapore basis, the first in over two weeks that gas oil has managed to breach the $23.00 mark.
Fuel oil swaps were down by $1.00 per tonne from Wednesday after physical sellers emerged on Wednesday for the first time in over a week to check the soaring swaps prices.
Swap prices had over the past week risen by over $5.00 per tonne on strong bunker demand.
August and September swaps were last quoted at $103.00/$103.75 per tonne, from Wednesday's $103.75/$104.50, brokers said.
Both months traded to a high of $104.50 per tonne on Wednesday, they said.
August naphtha was last quoted at $21.75/$21.90 per barrel, down from Wednesday's $22.10/$22.25, brokers said.
